statement:
A proposal distribution (also termed a biased distribution, sample distribution, or biasing density, denoted with density or mass function $g(x)$ or $f_*(x)$, or probability measure $\mathbb{Q}$) is an alternative distribution from which samples are generated instead of the distribution of interest $f(x)$ (or measure $\mathbb{P}$), defined such that expectations under $\mathbb{P}$ are evaluated via likelihood-ratio weighted samples under $\mathbb{Q}$:
$$\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}}[X] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}\left[\frac{X}{Y}\right] \quad \text{or} \quad \mathbb{E}[1_{\{X \ge t\}}] = \int 1_{\{x \ge t\}} \frac{f(x)}{f_*(x)} f_*(x)\,dx = \mathbb{E}_*[1_{\{X \ge t\}} W(X)]$$
where $W(X) \equiv \frac{f(X)}{g(X)}$ (or $\frac{f(X)}{f_*(X)}$) is the likelihood ratio / weighting function.

symbols.meaning: probability density (or mass) function of the biased, proposal, or sample distribution
probability density (or mass) function of the desired target distribution
biasing density function for the simulation experiment
weighting function / likelihood ratio defined as f(X)/g(X) or f(X)/f_*(X)
alternative probability measure defined for importance sampling

properties.property: Unbiased estimation via likelihood ratio weighting: $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}}[X] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[X/Y]$ and $\mathbb{E}[\hat{p}_t] = p_t$
properties.why: Weighting simulation outputs by the likelihood ratio $W(X) = f(X)/g(X)$ corrects for the use of the biased distribution

properties.property: Variance reduction condition: estimation precision is improved when $\operatorname{var}_{\mathbb{Q}}[X/Y] < \operatorname{var}_{\mathbb{P}}[X]$
properties.why: The proposal distribution redistributes probability mass to sample more frequently from regions where input variables have greater impact

properties.property: Optimal proposal density: $g^*(X) = \frac{|X|f(X)}{\int |x|f(x)\,dx}$ minimizes $\operatorname{var}_g\left(X\frac{f(X)}{g(X)}\right)$, achieving zero variance when $X \geq 0$
properties.why: Sampling under $g^*(X)$ scales the sample to be constant

properties.property: Biasing via scaling: $f_*(x) = \frac{1}{a} f(x/a)$ with weighting function $W(x) = a \frac{f(x)}{f(x/a)}$ for $a > 1$
properties.why: Positive scaling increases the variance and creates heavier tails, shifting probability mass into the tail event region $X \ge t$

assumptions.assumption: Non-zero density / support coverage: $Y(\omega) \neq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-almost everywhere (or $g(x) > 0$ wherever $f(x) > 0$)
assumptions.breaks_when: The proposal distribution assigns zero density/probability to regions where the target distribution has non-zero probability, making the likelihood ratio $f(X)/g(X)$ or $X/Y$ undefined or dividing by zero

assumptions.assumption: Proper normalization: $Y \ge 0$ with $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}}[Y] = 1$, and $g(x)$ is a valid density integrating to 1
assumptions.breaks_when: $Y < 0$ or $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}}[Y] \neq 1$, which biases the expectation estimate

failure_modes.signature: $\operatorname{var}_{\mathbb{Q}}[X/Y] \ge \operatorname{var}_{\mathbb{P}}[X]$, resulting in slower convergence and longer simulation run times than standard Monte Carlo
failure_modes.cause: Poor choice of proposal distribution $g$ that fails to encourage important regions or assigns low probabilities to high-impact values

failure_modes.signature: Importance sampling gain decreases as the dimension $n$ grows
failure_modes.cause: Scaling spreads probability mass into the complementary non-target region across an $n$-dimensional space when $X$ is a sum of $n$ random variables
